mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the head and spine to the trunk was most worthwhile: it showed how nerves and blood routes reach the same muscles, connecting several earlier ideas.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the two named lower-body slots was clear but a little repetitive; the main decision was simply which organ to place first.

surprise.text: The final view showed that skin and marrow keep making replacement cells, so assembly did not mean the body had stopped changing.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, though the order of the two lower-body fittings was a choice without an obvious biological consequence.

continue.text: I would be curious to continue if another chapter explored how the assembled systems respond together, though this chapter's mostly directed placements were less engaging as puzzles.
